title: Back into the Depression and organizing a new band
summary: Wooding returns during the Depression, which Harlem hardly noticed, and forms a band with Sid Catlett, Frankie Newton, Albert Nicholas and Bernard Addison.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Right. You came back right into the depression. As, I think, we were about to go into the worst year of the depression.

But by this time here -- but I didn't mind it, because we didn't mind it in Harlem at all because, it's like some of the fellows said, 'We've always been in a depression.' So, it didn't bother us At All. (laugh)
So, what did you do when you came back?

Well, I started organizing a band. After awhile I organized a band and I had in the band such men as Big Catlett Sid Catley. I had Frankie Newton. I had Nicholas Red Nichols. And then the first band, Bushell Butch Elber was with me and Cedric, they came
back with me. And then was, I don't know, not Johnny Mitchell, he stayed over there. I had Bernard on the guitar, and I had --

Yeah. And I had the makings of a better band than I had. Had we been able to go. But in those days, there was no go because if you didn't have a radio network in your place, it wasn't going. A man named Levy, he tried to open a place in Long Island and have us there, but somehow he couldn't get the liquor license or something. Anyhow, Levy was a man that had Eddie Johnson up at a place that later on became the Cotton Club, you know?
Oh, right. So what did you do? Did you get any jobs?
What do you call when you just, I freelanced.
